sections.heading: Putting this day into your hands
sections.text: Almighty God, Father, I’m stepping into this day now. I give myself to you—my mind, my body, my work, my responsibilities, and the people I love. Please watch over me, keep me, lead me, correct me, make me holy, and bless what is good. Turn my heart toward your ways before the day pulls me in other directions.
theological_themes: Beginning the day by entrusting the whole self and all circumstances to God’s care
Dependence on God for guidance, protection, and sanctifying grace

scripture_references.connection: This passage calls God’s people to trust him rather than their own understanding and to acknowledge him in all their ways. That directly supports the prayer’s morning surrender of plans, relationships, and decisions to God’s direction.
The psalm presents the Lord as the keeper of his people in all their coming and going. It grounds the request that God would watch over and preserve the person throughout the day.

sections.heading: Make me more like Jesus
sections.text: Shape me today into the likeness of Jesus. I know I am not finished, and I cannot make myself holy by willpower. Form me the way a potter works clay—patiently, firmly, and completely. Let my words be tuned to praise you instead of serving my pride, impatience, or fear.
theological_themes: Sanctification as God’s work of conforming believers to Christ
Human dependence on God’s transforming power
Speech offered to God in worship rather than self-centeredness

scripture_references.connection: Paul describes God’s saving purpose as conforming believers to the image of his Son. This supports the prayer’s request to be shaped into Christlikeness rather than merely improved outwardly.
This passage connects beholding the Lord with being transformed into his image by the Spirit. It fits the prayer’s desire for inward change that God himself accomplishes.

sections.heading: Let my life show that I belong to you
sections.text: Let the people around me see the work of your Spirit in me. Keep me from being dazzled by the world’s empty promises. Renew my mind so I don’t simply absorb the patterns around me. Dress me for the spiritual battle I actually face, and make my life a steady light—not loud or showy, but clear, faithful, and clean in what I do.
theological_themes: Visible holiness as the fruit of the Spirit’s work
Resistance to worldly values and false promises
Spiritual warfare and dependence on God’s armor
Christian witness through a faithful life

scripture_references.connection: Paul urges believers not to be conformed to this world but transformed by the renewal of the mind. That closely matches the prayer’s concern to resist worldly vanities and live from a renewed inner life.
This passage describes the believer’s need for the whole armor of God in spiritual conflict. It supports the prayer’s request to be prepared and protected in the unseen battle of the day.

Jesus calls his disciples the light of the world and connects visible good works with the Father’s glory. This grounds the prayer’s desire to shine faithfully before others without seeking self-display.

sections.heading: Keep me clean in messy places
sections.text: Please don’t let evil settle into my thoughts, my words, or my actions today. If I have to walk through difficult, muddy, compromised places, keep my life from being stained by them. Guard what I look at, what I want, what I say, and what I choose when no one is watching.
theological_themes: Personal holiness in thought, speech, and action
Persevering in purity while living in a fallen world
Need for God’s keeping power against sin

scripture_references.connection: The psalm asks how a young person can keep his way pure and answers by keeping it according to God’s word. It supports the prayer’s desire for practical purity in the paths of daily life.
Paul prays that God would sanctify believers completely and keep their whole person blameless. This aligns with the prayer’s request that thoughts, words, and deeds be kept from defilement.

sections.heading: Help me live today in light of eternity
sections.text: When I deal with ordinary business, conversations, money, plans, and deadlines, keep my deepest love anchored in heaven. Open my eyes to how fragile and temporary this world is when it tries to become my treasure. Teach me to see today in the light of eternity, to wait for Jesus, to listen for the final call, and to long for the new heaven and new earth where righteousness is at home.
theological_themes: Heavenly-mindedness in ordinary earthly responsibilities
The temporary nature of worldly vanities
Hope in Christ’s return and the new creation
Living now in view of eternity

scripture_references.connection: Paul tells believers who have been raised with Christ to seek the things above, where Christ is, while still living on earth. This supports the prayer’s desire for heavenly affection in the middle of ordinary responsibilities.
Peter connects the coming renewal of all things with lives of holiness and godliness now. This grounds the prayer’s longing for the new heavens and new earth and its call to live today in that light.
Paul speaks of the final trumpet and the transformation of believers at Christ’s victory over death. This directly supports the prayer’s watchful listening for the final trumpet call.

sections.heading: Make my words and steps count
sections.text: Please order every conversation today by your wisdom. Let what I say and receive actually do good. Don’t let me waste people’s time or my own soul. Make me someone who is helped by others and useful to them. Teach me to speak as if my words matter, and to walk as if each step is a gift I may not get again.
theological_themes: Godly speech that builds others up
Mutual edification in relationships
Wisdom in daily conduct
Awareness of life’s brevity

scripture_references.connection: Paul instructs believers to speak only what builds up and gives grace to those who hear. This supports the prayer’s request that each conversation be governed by wisdom and be useful for mutual good.
This passage links wise conduct with gracious, fitting speech. It illuminates the prayer’s concern that daily communications be purposeful, gracious, and beneficial.
Moses asks God to teach his people to number their days so they may gain wisdom. This supports the prayer’s desire to treat words and steps seriously because life is brief.

sections.heading: If this is my last day
sections.text: Father, if my life ends today, let this be a day I spend close to you. Let it be my most faithful day, my most honest day, my most loving day, my most awake day. Keep me ready to meet you—not trusting in myself, but in Christ—and let this day be used fully for your glory.
theological_themes: Readiness for death without morbid fear
Faithfulness in the present day
Trust in Christ rather than self at the end of life
Desire that one’s final day would glorify God

scripture_references.connection: Paul frames both life and death around Christ being honored in him. This supports the prayer’s desire that even if life ends today, the day would be lived faithfully for God’s glory.
James warns against presuming on tomorrow and teaches believers to live under the Lord’s will. This grounds the prayer’s sober recognition that the present day is not guaranteed.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original’s language about “trampling the world underfoot” could be misunderstood as contempt for creation or ordinary earthly duties. I rendered it as resistance to the world’s empty promises while preserving the biblical idea of nonconformity to fallen worldly patterns.

The strong contrast between heaven and earth reflects a Puritan emphasis on eternity and the vanity of worldly things. I kept that force but avoided implying that embodied life, work, relationships, or creation are evil in themselves.
significant_interpretive_choices: I interpreted “affection be in heaven” and “view all things in the mirror of eternity” as a call to heavenly-mindedness within ordinary responsibilities, not withdrawal from daily life.
I rendered “profited or made profitable” as being helped by others and useful to them, since the original seems to mean mutual spiritual benefit rather than financial gain.
I kept the final request, “If my life should end today, let this be my best day,” as readiness and faithfulness before God rather than a request for earthly success or emotional happiness.
